brief: Middle East de-escalation pushed the physical oil market into surplus, dropping Brent almost 20% in a fortnight to about $96/bbl, near JPM's fair value. Separately, an abrupt AI de-risking/momentum unwind hit risk assets, initially rallying DM bonds on hopes of limited further Fed tightening. That hope was challenged: October payrolls rebounded to 159k (3-month average 137k, highest since May) and October CPI ran hot (0.35% m/m headline, 0.30% core), while Fed officials (Waller, Logan, Paulson hawkish; Bowman the moderating voice) leaned toward more tightening. JPM's baseline stays a 25bp December hike, but the market now prices over three more hikes by September 2027 (cumulative pricing repriced to about 90bp from about 47bp in a week), raising the risk of a shift from a patient Fed to a price-stability-focused one, possibly as soon as December's FOMC. JPM reads the AI selloff (momentum crowding down from the 100th to 76th percentile, -38.4% drawdown) as a healthy positioning reset, not a broken supercycle, reiterating its S&P 500 8,000 target and hyperscaler-over-high-beta-AI preference. Equity broadening needs Fed hikes resolved, strong earnings (Q3 EPS beats: US +24% y/y, Europe +28%) and midterm clarity (Democrats won Congress); two of three hurdles have eased, but sticky inflation keeps JPM out of the broadening camp for now.
